title: Sales Enablement Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference’s positioning and messaging, competitive battlecards, pitch/deck guidance, pricing guidance, exemplar case studies, and a concise security FAQ for prospect conversations. It is intended for AE/SDRs/SEs, solutions engineers, and GTM leaders to run discovery, handle objections, and close deals for Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Audience: Sales, Solution Engineering, Sales Enablement, Partner Success.

Quick links
- Positioning & elevator pitch
- Competitive brief & battlecards
- Pitch deck structure and slide notes
- Pricing guidance and examples
- Case study template + examples

1) Positioning & Core Messaging

Executive summary (one-liner)
- Redwood Inference: a developer-first inference platform that makes production LLM serving predictable, cost-effective, and reliable across hosted, dedicated, and private environments.

Problem we solve
- Customers struggle to deliver LLM features in production because of unpredictable latency, high unit costs, operational complexity, and model lifecycle risk.

How we win (pillars)
- Production-first performance: GPU-optimized runtime, continuous batching, KV/prefix caching to hit strict latency SLOs.
- Unified footprint: same API and rollout tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Cost controls: intelligent batching, quantization profiles, and routing policies that reduce per-token costs without sacrificing quality.
- Operational visibility: per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and regression alerting tied to prompt sets.

Elevator pitches
- Tech (15s): "Redwood gives engineers one API to run models anywhere — hosted, reserved GPU pools, or private VPCs — while delivering predictable latency, transparent costs, and built-in rollouts and monitoring."
- Business (30s): "Teams use Redwood to get LLM features shipped quickly and run them at scale with predictable costs and enterprise controls — so product teams avoid spending months tuning infrastructure and instead focus on product quality."

Differentiators (talking points)
- Model-agnostic serving runtime with kernel selection and quantization-aware execution.
- Transparent performance profiles in our model catalog (latency/throughput/ideal batch sizes).
- Fallback and routing policies (latency/cost/region) for graceful degradation.
- Built-in quality guardrails: evals + regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

2) Competitive Briefs & Battlecards

Competitive themes to call out in discovery
- Cost vs. quality tradeoffs and who owns the optimization burden.
- Deployment flexibility (can they satisfy VPC/on-prem needs with same tooling?).
- Observability granularity (token-level, per-route insights, QA-driven regression alerts).
- Reliability/fallback strategy when capacity is constrained.

Top competitors (example) and quick positioning
- Cloud vendor managed endpoints (AWS/Azure/GCP): 
  - Strengths: deep infra integration, global regions.
  - Weaknesses: endpoint variability across regions, limited model catalog, less developer-friendly rollout tooling.
  - Redwood pitch: "We give a single API and consistent performance/rollout UX across environments; customers can run the same workloads with predictable economics."
- Large LLM API providers: 
  - Strengths: simple APIs and large model footprints.
  - Weaknesses: opacity on performance/cost breakdowns, fewer deployment options for regulated customers.
  - Redwood pitch: "We provide transparent per-token cost and latency, and enterprise deployment modes for regulated workloads."
- Self-hosted runtime vendors / OSS serving stacks: 
  - Strengths: control and lower marginal cost at scale.
  - Weaknesses: engineering burden, slower feature velocity, less curated model onboarding.
  - Redwood pitch: "We combine a curated runtime and operational tooling so platform teams get control without rebuilding the stack."

Battlecard (one-slide cheat sheet)
- Use case fit: rapid prototyping (Hosted), predictable production workloads (Dedicated), regulated/air-gapped (Private).
- Objection handling: "We already use cloud endpoints" -> show cost/latency comparison + unique features (rollouts, prefix caching).
- Key metrics to probe: SLOs (P95 latency), tokens/sec per GPU, allowed data residency, SLA needs.

3) Pitch Deck Structure & Slide Notes

Recommended sequence (10–12 slides)
1. Title + value statement (customized to prospect)
2. Customer problem (quantified: cost / latency / incidents)
3. Redwood solution overview (one-liner + architecture diagram)
4. How it works (serving runtime + orchestration + routing)
5. Deployment options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) with a short decision guide
6. Performance & cost evidence (benchmarks vs public alternatives, typical token costs)
7. Security & compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC support, audit logging)
8. Case study (relevant customer with outcome metrics)
9. Pricing overview (tiers, reserved commits, add-ons)
10. Rollout & support plan (onboarding, integration, SLA)
11. Next steps & ask (POC, pilot terms, security review)

Slide notes & tips
- Start with a prospect-specific quant ("Our customers reduced per-token cost by X% after applying Redwood Optimize").
- Use a single architecture diagram highlighting the same API surface across deployment modes.
- Include a succinct appendix: SLOs, supported models, integration checklist, sample responses.

4) Pricing Guidance & Example Scenarios

Pricing principles
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token/per-embedding), tiered volume discounts, optional premium SLAs and observability add-ons.
- Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved capacity pricing (GPU pool-based) with commit levels and burst options.
- Private: license + support fee (enterprise), optional on-prem packaging.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, compliance packages, premium SLAs, training and evals.

Rules of thumb for quoting
- For early POCs: recommend Hosted with a consumption forecast and optional 3-month committed trial discount.
- For predictable production: propose Dedicated with a 12-month commit sized to target QPS and token volume; include burst and autoscale guardrails.
- For regulated: price Private as license + deployment services; include professional services for onboarding and security review.

Example pricing scenarios (illustrative, not contractual)
- SaaS startup POC: Hosted — 5M tokens/month; sticker: $0.0015 / token -> $7,500/mo; propose 20% trial discount for first 3 months.
- Mid-market product team: Dedicated — 2x A100-equivalent GPU pool reserved; base fee $35k/mo; includes 24/7 support and 99.9% uptime SLA.
- Enterprise regulated customer: Private — $250k one-time license + $15k/mo support + $120k deployment services (security and integration).

Pricing negotiation levers
- Commit term (month vs annual)
- Burst and autoscale limits
- Observability retention period
- Quantization/Optimize profiles or eval packages

5) Case Study Template & Example

Template (use for written case studies)
- Title: One-line result (customer + outcome)
- Customer background: industry, size, deployment mode used
- Challenge: specifics (latency, cost, reliability, compliance)
- Solution: Redwood components deployed and rollout approach
- Results: numeric outcomes (latency P95 improvements, % cost reduction, time-to-production)
- Quote and next steps

Example case study: 'Atlas Payments — Reduced fraud-model latency and cost'
- Customer background: Atlas Payments, mid-market fintech, US-based, PCI scope
- Challenge: fraud scoring model p95 latency at peak was 700ms causing checkout friction; cost of model inferencing spiked during peak trading hours.
- Solution: Dedicated deployment with prefix caching for user history, optimized quantization profile for fraud model, routing policy to fall back to a smaller variant under high load, and integration with Atlas SSO and KMS.
- Results: P95 latency dropped from 700ms to 160ms; monthly inference cost decreased by 46%; time-to-production for model rollout reduced from 8 weeks to 3 weeks; no security incidents in first 12 months.
- Customer quote: "Redwood let us run production inference reliably and cut costs in half — we could focus on model quality, not infra."

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (short answers for SEs and AEs)

Q: What compliance certifications do you have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. We provide artifacts during security reviews under NDA and have a documented compliance roadmap for ISO 27001 and FedRAMP readiness for specific customers.

Q: How is customer data protected in Hosted?
A: Data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3) and at rest. Access to customer data in the control plane is restricted by RBAC and logged. We offer per-customer encryption keys via KMS for additional separation.

Q: Do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) / customer-managed KMS?
A: Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM integrations in Private setups.

Q: How do you isolate tenant workloads on Dedicated?
A: Dedicated customers get isolated GPU pools, network segmentation, per-tenant quotas, and strict tenancy controls at the routing layer. Logs and metrics can be partitioned and sent to customer-owned destinations.

Q: Can Redwood be deployed on-prem or in a VPC?
A: Yes — Private offers a customer VPC deployment or on-prem package. We provide reference architectures and a professional services engagement for air-gapped installs.

Q: What logging, auditing, and traceability do you provide?
A: We provide audit logs for model deployments, API key usage, admin actions, and access events. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, S3) and we support distributed tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry).

Q: How are vulnerabilities handled?
A: We maintain an internal vulnerability management process with triage SLAs, patch windows, and coordinated disclosures. For Private deployments we offer customers a CVE tracker and scheduled patching cadence options.

Q: What contractual protections (SLA/penalties) exist?
A: For Dedicated and Private customers we provide SLA commitments (uptime & latency tiers). SLAs and remedies are negotiated as part of the contract; standard Hosted customers receive our public SLA page details.

Q: How do you ensure model and inference integrity?
A: We offer model-signing and version pinning, immutable model artifacts in the catalog, and policy-based rollouts with automatic rollback on regression alerts. Customers can run evals against production prompts before full rollout.

Q: Do you retain request/response payloads?
A: By default, logs are retained for troubleshooting and billing; retention windows depend on plan. Customers can request reduced retention, no-retention modes, or direct log forwarding to their storage.

7) Sales Playbook: Discovery Checklist & Qualification Questions

Technical fit questions
- What are your latency SLOs (P95 and P99)?
- What QPS / tokens-per-second do you expect at peak?
- Are you planning inference on user data that requires residency or special handling?
- Do you need private networking (VPC) or on-prem deployment?

Commercial fit questions
- What is your expected monthly token/embedding volume?
- Do you prefer usage-based billing or reserved capacity?
- What is your procurement and security-review timeline?

Decision criteria to probe
- Cost per token vs model quality tradeoff, deployment control, observability, enterprise SLAs, and time-to-shipping.
